_readme: THE BORE AT THE MOUTH (2026-10-26, Mark: "a rolling wave on the coast"). The 1 km event of impact_newburyport_1km.json,
the eye on the north jetty's tip looking out to sea, 12 m up, from 19:55Z through the train's peak at 30x: the surge
comes over the bar into the standing water of the inlet as a BORE -- a jump of metres over tens of metres -- and the
bank kernel feeds its face to the crest law (the cusp, the roller, the flight where the bed is steep), the column
plane folds where the labels overtake, and its whitewater is Belanger's. Over the dry marsh the surge runs as a thin
tongue and shows no face; the bore forms on water. Then the eye rises to 60 m over the inlet.
